title: Microsoft Is Building a 3,600-Km Undersea Cable From India to Singapore. The AI Data Race Just Went Submarine.
excerpt: A consortium led by Lightstorm, backed by Microsoft, Tata Communications, Singtel, and NEC, will lay the I-2SEA cable to feed India's exploding demand for AI and cloud bandwidth — landing it in the same Andhra Pradesh town where Meta and Google are building data centers.
body:
India's race to become a global AI hub just acquired its newest piece of critical infrastructure — and it runs along the ocean floor.

A consortium that includes **Microsoft**, Singapore-based telecom startup **Lightstorm**, **Tata Communications**, **Singapore Telecommunications (Singtel)**, Singapore's **ASEAN Cableship**, and Japan's **NEC Corporation** announced on Thursday that they will build the **I-2SEA cable**, a 3,600-kilometre submarine fiber optic link connecting India with Malaysia and Singapore.

The cable is designed to carry AI, cloud, and hyperscale workloads between India and Southeast Asia — two of the world's fastest-growing data markets. It is expected to be operational by the fourth quarter of 2029.

## Landing in India's Newest Data Center Corridor

The I-2SEA cable will have landing stations in **Machilipatnam**, a coastal town in the southern Indian state of Andhra Pradesh. The location is no accident: both **Meta** and **Alphabet's Google** have already announced major data center projects in the same region, effectively turning the Andhra coast into India's next digital infrastructure corridor.

Lightstorm, the consortium's anchor partner, currently connects 19 AI and cloud zones across India through its terrestrial fiber cable networks. The I-2SEA cable is expected to bring that number to 29, according to **Amajit Gupta**, the company's CEO and Managing Director.

> **"The I Squared-backed startup is also planning an IPO in India by mid-2027, with a reported target valuation of up to **$1.5 billion**."**

The I Squared-backed startup is also planning an IPO in India by mid-2027, with a reported target valuation of up to **$1.5 billion**.

## Why This Matters Now

Undersea cables carry roughly **95% of the world's internet traffic**. India currently has 17 active submarine cables with a maximum potential capacity of 960 terabits per second, and at least 10 more have been publicly announced, according to **TeleGeography**, a telecommunications research firm.

The I-2SEA announcement comes as hyperscalers are pouring tens of billions into Indian data infrastructure. Amazon recently committed an additional **$13 billion** to expand AI data centers in Mumbai and Hyderabad, bringing its total India investment to **$48 billion** between 2026 and 2030. Microsoft itself earmarked **$17.5 billion** for Indian AI infrastructure last year, and Google has pledged **$15 billion** over five years for data centers in southern India.

India's operational data center capacity stands at about **1.4 gigawatts** today. According to **Macquarie Equity Research**, that figure could double by 2027 and increase five-fold by 2030 if planned projects are fast-tracked.

## Tata Communications' Parallel Push

The I-2SEA cable is part of a broader subsea buildout by Tata Communications, which separately announced **$152 million** in investments across two India-Singapore cable projects. The first — the **MIST cable system** connecting Mumbai and Singapore — will cost $63 million and add 20 Tbps of capacity, with service expected by Q4 FY27. The second — **Project CS**, linking Chennai and Singapore — will cost $89 million, add 78 Tbps, and come online by Q3 FY31.

Tata Communications already operates an installed subsea network capacity of about **270 Tbps**, of which 172 Tbps is currently lit. "As global demand for digital and AI-driven services continues to accelerate, these investments reinforce our commitment to building future-ready digital infrastructure at scale," said **Genius Wong**, the company's Executive VP and CTO.

## The Diaspora Angle

For the millions of NRIs working in tech across Singapore, Southeast Asia, and the United States, this infrastructure buildout isn't abstract. Lower-latency, higher-bandwidth connections between India and global AI hubs mean faster enterprise applications, more competitive Indian cloud services, and a stronger case for multinational companies to process data through Indian infrastructure rather than routing it elsewhere.

The I-2SEA cable also signals that India's digital infrastructure ambitions are no longer confined to domestic fiber rollouts and 5G auctions. The country is now competing at the submarine cable layer — the literal backbone of the global internet — alongside the likes of the U.S., China, and the Gulf states.
